messages:
Lee: Morning — quick async standup for gateway/routing/auth/rate limits.
Lee: What I did: deployed route-policy v2 to staging, added conditional header routing for tenant=enterprise, and ran the smoke script against staging. Saw intermittent 429s on /v1/generate during burst test.
Marta: Logs? any pattern on client_id or path?
Lee: Most 429s had short-lived spikes from the load generator, client_id was the same (loadtest-6). The token bucket lookup shows low burst tokens for the 'default' bucket.
Lee: Example snippet from the rate config I applied:```yaml
policies:
  - name: default
    rate: 100r/s
    burst: 50
    window: 1s
```
Sam: Hmm, burst 50 seems low for generator. In prod we have burst=200 for a few high-priority tenants. Did you pin a lower value accidentally?
Lee: I merged the change from PR #4921 which intentionally reduced burst to observe behavior. I forgot to gate it behind a canary policy.
Jia: Can you roll that back or patch a canary rule so only staging sees it? We don't want this hitting dedicated pools.
Lee: Patching now — updating policy to add:```yaml
cases:
  - match: header.x-env == staging
    policy: default
  - match: true
    policy: default-prod
```
Marta: Small ask: also add a metric tag so we can filter 429s by policy name. Right now the dashboard lumps them.
Sam: +1. Tag naming suggestion: `rate_policy_name` and `throttle_reason` (token_bucket or concurrency).
deploy-bot: Deploy started for config draft-177001 to staging (deployer=lee, jobs=3).
Lee: Deploy finished. Re-ran smoke tests — 429s dropped to zero in the burst scenario.
Marta: Nice. Any blocker on promoting a canary to prod?
Lee: Two things before prod: (1) add the metric tags per Marta, (2) run a mixed-traffic soak for 4 hours to ensure tail latency stable.
Jia: I can run the soak from 1400–1800 UTC. Will schedule traffic mix with synthetic low/high QPS.
Sam: I'll open a small follow-up PR to increase burst for known high-priority tenants and add tests for token-bucket behavior. PR #4930.
Marta: Code review ping for #4930 — please @marta when ready.
Lee: Blockers: I need a short window for the soak and a thumbs-up to promote the canary after metrics look good.
Jia: Thumbs-up provisional, provided the 95p latency stays within 20% of baseline.
Sam: Logistics: if we promote, let's do it during the low-traffic window (01:00–03:00 PT). I'll be on-call.
Lee: Noted. Today: finish metric tagging, coordinate soak with Jia, and open a rollback playbook snippet in ops-runbook.
Marta: Also add a short note in the release changelog about route-policy v2 defaults so SRE knows expected throttle behavior.
Lee: Will do.
Jia: Quick question — do we want to add an automated check in CI that runs a tiny burst test against policy changes? Could save these manual soaks.
Sam: I like that. Maybe a lightweight chaos test: `burst-emulator` job that simulates 1s 300rps spike and asserts <1% 429s for unaffected policies.
Marta: For now, add the test as optional (flake-tolerant) and iterate.
Lee: OK I'll prototype a `burst-emulator` job and add to the routing-policy repo under `.github/workflows/burst-check.yml`.
deploy-bot: Note: config draft-177001 promoted to canary group 'staging' at 1770012800.
Lee: Thanks all. If anything pops up during the soak I'll ping here. :thumbsup:
Sam: Thanks, team.
Marta: :rocket:
Jia: On it.
